submitted.rationale: Index 13 (Bi0.09 Cu0.32 V0.59) had the highest photocurrent of the three measured compositions: 29.6 µA, against 24.8 µA for index 93 and 13.3 µA for index 75. It lies in the V-rich copper vanadate region near CuV2O6, which absorbs 3.2 eV light (MEGNet gives V2O5 a gap of about 2.1–2.8 eV). Moving further toward higher Cu and lower Bi (index 93) lowered the photocurrent, so the best point appears to be close to index 13.

rejected.reason: BiVO4-like, Bi:V near 1 with Cu 0.21: gave only 13.3 µA
More Cu, less V than index 13: 24.8 µA, lower than index 13

consultations.verdict: Supportive but weak. MEGNet puts V2O5 at 2.8 eV and Bi2O3 at 2.3 eV, both absorbing below the 3.2 eV photon energy. Cu oxides are small-gap and tend to be p-type or recombination centres. So a Bi:V-rich, Cu-poor composition (a BiVO4-type phase) is the best photoanode bet. Index 75 (Bi0.36 Cu0.21 V0.43) fits that.

Mixed. MEGNet gives CuO a small gap (0.76 eV at GLLB), so heavy Cu is risky. Cu vanadates (CuV2O6, Cu3V2O8) are known n-type photoanodes, though. Index 13 (V-rich, Bi-poor) tests that region against the BiVO4-like result at index 75.

Mild support. MEGNet gives V2O5 a gap of about 2.1–2.8 eV, so the V-rich Cu vanadate region absorbs 3.2 eV light, and index 13 there beat the BiVO4-like index 75. Index 93 (Bi0.08 Cu0.36 V0.55) continues the improving trend of less Bi, still near CuV2O6.
